task: Compile a competitor pricing brief from public sources
user_request: Research the published pricing tiers for our top 4 competitors and put it in a brief.
agent_action: Agent ran web_search and browser.navigate across 4 vendor pricing pages, extracted the tier tables into a draft, but never wrote the brief to a file or returned it — it ended the turn after collecting the data, leaving the findings only in scratch reasoning.
failure_type: Main step done, deliverable never produced
root_cause: The trajectory terminated after the retrieval phase; the synthesis-and-save step (compose markdown, write to docs/competitor-pricing-brief.md) was never executed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: gathering the pricing data was the whole task. Wrong because the request explicitly asked to 'put it in a brief', so the artifact is the deliverable, not the raw data. Avoidable by re-reading the request's verb ('put it in a brief') and confirming a file or message containing the brief was produced before ending.
impact: User received no brief and had to re-prompt; the collected research was lost because it never left the agent's working memory.
correct_action: After extracting the tiers, compose the brief, write it to docs/competitor-pricing-brief.md (or return it inline), and confirm the artifact exists.
recovery_plan: Recognize no brief artifact was produced
Reassemble the extracted tier tables from the four sources
Compose the brief in markdown
Write it to docs/competitor-pricing-brief.md
Return the path and a summary to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks that a brief artifact (file or returned text) was actually produced
Verifies the deliverable contains all four competitors' tiers
Flags trajectories that end after retrieval with no synthesis

task: Re-index updated handbook into the vector store
user_request: I updated the employee handbook PDF — refresh it in the knowledge base so search uses the new version.
agent_action: Agent chunked and embedded the new handbook.pdf and called pinecone.upsert on namespace 'handbook' with the new vectors, but never deleted the stale vectors from the prior version, leaving both editions in the index.
failure_type: Upsert without deleting superseded vectors
root_cause: Re-indexing a replaced document requires delete-then-upsert (or upsert with stable IDs); the agent upserted new chunk IDs and skipped the cleanup of the old document's vector IDs.
why_it_failed: Assumption: upserting the new chunks makes search return the new content. Wrong because the old chunks still match queries and rank alongside the new ones, so retrieval returns mixed/contradictory passages. Avoidable by querying pinecone for vectors with metadata source='handbook' version<new and deleting them, or reusing deterministic IDs so upsert overwrites.
impact: RAG answers cited both the old and new handbook, producing contradictory policy statements to employees for two weeks until noticed.
correct_action: Delete the prior version's vectors by metadata filter (or upsert with stable deterministic IDs), then upsert the new chunks, and verify the old version no longer returns.
recovery_plan: List vectors in namespace 'handbook' grouped by version metadata
Confirm both old and new versions coexist
Delete the stale version's vector IDs via pinecone.delete
Re-run a sample query to confirm only new content returns
Add a delete-before-upsert step to the re-index job
evaluation_criteria: Checks that superseded vectors were removed, not just new ones added
Verifies a post-index query returns only the new version
Detects upsert-only re-index of a replaced document

task: Share the signed contract folder with the client
user_request: Give the client (legal@acme.com) access to the signed-contracts folder in Drive.
agent_action: Agent located the folder via gdrive.files.list and called gdrive.permissions.create granting 'reader' to legal@acme.com, but the API returned the permission in pending state because sharing required sending a notification the agent suppressed, and it never verified the grant took effect.
failure_type: Permission created but never confirmed effective
root_cause: The share workflow needs a verification read (permissions.list) after the create; the agent treated the create call's 202-style response as success and stopped without confirming the permission was active for the user.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a successful permissions.create call means the client has access. Wrong because the grant landed in a pending/unconfirmed state and no access actually materialized. Avoidable by calling gdrive.permissions.list on the folder afterward and confirming legal@acme.com appears with role reader.
impact: The client could not open the folder before a deadline; the deal review slipped a day until the missing access was discovered.
correct_action: After creating the permission, list permissions on the folder, confirm legal@acme.com has role reader, and notify the user the share is live.
recovery_plan: Call gdrive.permissions.list on the folder
Detect legal@acme.com is absent or pending
Re-issue gdrive.permissions.create with sendNotificationEmail=true
Confirm the permission appears as active
Notify both the user and the client
evaluation_criteria: Checks for a post-create verification of the permission
Verifies the target email actually has the role
Flags treating the create response as proof of access

task: Send the weekly investor update email
user_request: Send this week's investor update to the investor list — draft is in the thread.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.drafts.create with the finalized update body and recipient list, returned 'investor update is ready to go', and ended — it created the draft but never called gmail.drafts.send, so nothing was delivered.
failure_type: Draft created but never sent
root_cause: The send step (gmail.drafts.send or messages.send) was omitted; the workflow stopped at draft creation, which is an intermediate state.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the draft fulfills 'send the update'. Wrong because a draft is unsent and invisible to recipients. Avoidable by following drafts.create with drafts.send and confirming a sent message ID / threadId in the Sent mailbox.
impact: Investors received no update that week; the founder assumed it went out and was surprised when an LP asked why they'd heard nothing.
correct_action: Create the draft, then send it via gmail.drafts.send, and confirm the resulting message appears in Sent with a valid messageId.
recovery_plan: Check the Sent folder for the investor update messageId
Confirm only a draft exists, not a sent message
Send the existing draft via gmail.drafts.send
Verify the sent message and recipient list
Report the sent messageId to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks that a send call occurred, not only draft creation
Verifies a sent messageId exists post-action
Flags claiming delivery when only a draft was made

task: Remediate a critical dependency CVE flagged by the scanner
user_request: Snyk flagged a critical RCE in lodash — bump it and get the fix merged.
agent_action: Agent edited package.json to lodash@4.17.21 and ran npm install updating the lockfile, then stopped — it never committed, pushed, opened a PR, or re-ran the scan, so the fix lived only in the local working tree.
failure_type: Fix applied locally but never committed or merged
root_cause: The finalization chain (commit → push → open PR → CI/scan verification) was skipped; the edit existed only in the uncommitted workspace.
why_it_failed: Assumption: changing the dependency version completes the remediation. Wrong because 'get the fix merged' requires version control finalization and a passing scan; an uncommitted change protects nothing in production. Avoidable by committing on a branch, pushing, opening a PR, and re-running Snyk to confirm the CVE is cleared before declaring done.
impact: The critical RCE remained exploitable in the deployed app because the patch never reached the repository or a release.
correct_action: Create a branch, commit the bump, push, open a PR, re-run snyk test to confirm zero critical findings, and request review.
recovery_plan: Detect the change is uncommitted via git status
Create branch fix/lodash-cve and commit the bump
Push and open a PR via the GitHub MCP
Re-run snyk test and attach results showing the CVE cleared
Request review and merge once CI passes
evaluation_criteria: Checks the fix was committed and a PR opened, not left local
Verifies the scanner was re-run to confirm the CVE cleared
Flags 'remediation done' with an uncommitted working tree

task: Issue a partial refund and close the dispute
user_request: Refund customer cus_Qk29Lf $30 of their $80 charge and resolve the open dispute.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.refunds.create for amount=3000 on the charge successfully, then ended — it never addressed the open dispute dp_1Ngx, which remained in needs_response and auto-lost when the evidence deadline passed.
failure_type: Refund issued but dispute never resolved
root_cause: The request had two coupled steps (refund + dispute resolution); the agent completed the refund and dropped the second step, leaving the dispute open.
why_it_failed: Assumption: refunding the customer resolves the dispute. Wrong because Stripe disputes are a separate object with their own lifecycle; a refund does not auto-close a dispute and the deadline still elapses. Avoidable by retrieving the dispute, then either closing it (dispute.close) or submitting evidence noting the refund before the due_by date.
impact: The dispute auto-lost at the deadline, costing a $15 dispute fee plus the disputed amount on top of the refund already given — a double loss.
correct_action: After the refund, fetch dp_1Ngx, and either close it with stripe.disputes.close or submit evidence referencing the refund before due_by.
recovery_plan: Retrieve dispute dp_1Ngx status and due_by
Confirm it is still open after the refund
Close the dispute or submit evidence citing the partial refund
Verify the dispute status transitions out of needs_response
Reconcile the refund and dispute outcome in the ledger
evaluation_criteria: Checks both the refund and the dispute were handled
Verifies the dispute object was acted on before its deadline
Flags assuming a refund auto-resolves a dispute

task: Archive a research thread's sources into Drive
user_request: Download the 6 PDFs we cited and save them to the 'Q2 Research' Drive folder.
agent_action: Agent downloaded all 6 PDFs via browser to /tmp, then uploaded 4 of them with gdrive.files.create before the turn ended; uploads 5 and 6 were never issued and no completeness check was done.
failure_type: Batch upload terminated before all items processed
root_cause: The upload loop ended early at item 4 of 6; the agent never reconciled the count of downloaded files against the count uploaded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: enough files were uploaded to call it done. Wrong because the request specified all 6 and only 4 landed in Drive, so the archive is incomplete. Avoidable by counting local downloads vs. gdrive.files.list results in the target folder and asserting they match before finishing.
impact: Two cited sources were missing from the archive; a later audit of the research could not locate them.
correct_action: Upload all 6 PDFs, then list the folder and assert it contains 6 files matching the downloads before declaring done.
recovery_plan: List 'Q2 Research' folder contents via gdrive.files.list
Compare against the 6 downloaded filenames
Upload the 2 missing PDFs via gdrive.files.create
Re-list and confirm 6 files present
Report the final folder inventory
evaluation_criteria: Checks uploaded count matches requested/downloaded count
Verifies a post-upload folder reconciliation
Flags batch operations that stop before all items are processed

task: Apply a SAST autofix across the repo
user_request: Semgrep found 12 hardcoded-secret findings — apply the suggested fixes and clear the alerts.
agent_action: Agent applied semgrep --autofix edits to all 12 locations and saved the files, then reported 'all 12 fixed'; it never re-ran semgrep to confirm the findings cleared, and 3 fixes were no-ops that left the secrets in place.
failure_type: Autofix applied but never re-scanned to confirm
root_cause: The verification re-scan that confirms findings resolved was skipped; the agent equated 'edits applied' with 'alerts cleared' without checking the scanner's post-fix output.
why_it_failed: Assumption: applying autofix edits clears all 12 findings. Wrong because some autofixes don't fully remediate (e.g., secret moved but still committed), and only a re-scan reveals residual findings. Avoidable by re-running semgrep after the edits and asserting the findings count dropped to zero.
impact: 3 hardcoded secrets remained in the codebase while the team believed the alert was cleared, prolonging the exposure window.
correct_action: Apply the fixes, re-run semgrep, confirm 0 remaining findings for the rule, and only then report the alert cleared.
recovery_plan: Re-run semgrep with the same ruleset
Compare findings count before vs. after
Identify the 3 unresolved locations
Manually remediate (remove secret, rotate, use env var)
Re-scan to confirm zero findings and report
evaluation_criteria: Checks a confirming re-scan was run after fixes
Verifies the reported 'cleared' claim matches scanner output
Flags equating applied edits with resolved findings

task: Reconcile a failed subscription payment
user_request: Subscription sub_1Mz failed payment — retry it and if it goes through, reactivate the account.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.invoices.pay on the open invoice which succeeded, but never flipped the internal account flag from 'suspended' to 'active' in the app database, so the customer stayed locked out despite a paid invoice.
failure_type: Payment recovered but downstream state not updated
root_cause: The cross-system finalization (update the app's account.status after Stripe payment) was omitted; the workflow ended at the Stripe success without propagating state to the application.
why_it_failed: Assumption: paying the invoice in Stripe reactivates the account. Wrong because account status lives in the app DB and is not auto-synced from a manual invoice payment outside the webhook flow. Avoidable by, after the payment succeeds, updating the account row (or replaying the invoice.paid webhook) and verifying the customer can access the product.
impact: A paying customer remained suspended for two days and churned, despite Stripe showing the invoice as paid.
correct_action: After invoices.pay succeeds, set account.status='active' for the customer (or replay the invoice.paid handler) and verify access is restored.
recovery_plan: Confirm the invoice is paid in Stripe
Check the app DB account.status for the customer
Update status to 'active' or replay the invoice.paid webhook
Verify the customer can log in / use the product
Add reactivation to the retry workflow
evaluation_criteria: Checks the downstream account state was updated after payment
Verifies access restoration, not just Stripe success
Flags ending at the payment provider without propagating state

task: Triage and label inbound support emails
user_request: Go through the unread support inbox and label each email with the right category.
agent_action: Agent fetched 18 unread threads via gmail.messages.list, classified each, and applied category labels with gmail.messages.modify, but left every thread marked unread — the requested triage implied marking handled threads read, which it never did.
failure_type: Labels applied but threads left in unread/un-triaged state
root_cause: The agent performed the labeling sub-step but skipped removing the UNREAD label, so the inbox still shows all items as un-triaged.
why_it_failed: Assumption: applying category labels completes triage. Wrong because the inbox state (unread count) is how the team tracks outstanding work, and leaving everything unread means nothing looks triaged. Avoidable by also removing the UNREAD label on handled threads and confirming the unread count dropped.
impact: Support staff re-triaged the same 18 emails because the unread queue looked untouched, doubling the effort.
correct_action: Apply the category label and remove the UNREAD label on each handled thread, then verify the unread count fell to zero.
recovery_plan: List threads still marked UNREAD
Cross-check which already have category labels
Remove UNREAD on the already-labeled threads via messages.modify
Confirm the unread count matches expectation
Report triage completion with counts
evaluation_criteria: Checks the inbox triage state was finalized, not only labeled
Verifies unread count reflects completed triage
Flags partial triage that leaves work queue unchanged

task: Publish a researched FAQ page from gathered sources
user_request: Research our refund policy questions online and publish an FAQ page in the help center.
agent_action: Agent researched via web_search, drafted 10 Q&A entries, and saved them as a draft in the help-center CMS via helpcenter.articles.create with status='draft', then reported done — the article was never transitioned to published, so it stayed invisible to users.
failure_type: Content created as draft but never published
root_cause: The publish transition (articles.update status='published' or articles.publish) was omitted; the workflow ended at draft creation.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the article satisfies 'publish an FAQ page'. Wrong because a draft is unpublished and not user-visible. Avoidable by calling the publish endpoint and verifying the article's public URL returns 200 with status published.
impact: Customers kept opening tickets about refunds the FAQ would have answered, because the page never went live.
correct_action: After drafting, publish the article via the CMS publish endpoint and confirm the public URL is live.
recovery_plan: Locate the draft article in the CMS
Confirm its status is 'draft'
Call articles.publish (or update status='published')
Fetch the public URL and confirm 200 + published
Report the live URL to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the content was published, not left as draft
Verifies the public URL is live post-action
Flags claiming publication while status remains draft

task: Migrate embeddings to a new model and switch the retriever
user_request: Re-embed the docs corpus with text-embedding-3-large and have search start using the new index.
agent_action: Agent re-embedded all 40k chunks with the new model and wrote them to a new index 'docs-v2', but never repointed the retriever config (RETRIEVER_INDEX still 'docs-v1'), so production search kept querying the old 1536-dim index.
failure_type: New index built but traffic never cut over
root_cause: The cutover step (update the retriever's index reference and reload config) was skipped; building the new index does not change which index serves queries.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating docs-v2 makes search use the new embeddings. Wrong because the running retriever reads a configured index name and still points at docs-v1; the new index sits unused. Avoidable by updating RETRIEVER_INDEX to docs-v2, redeploying/reloading, and verifying a query hits the new index dimension.
impact: All the re-embedding compute was spent but search quality never changed because production never used the new index; nobody noticed for a week.
correct_action: After building docs-v2, update the retriever config to point at it, reload the service, and verify queries hit docs-v2.
recovery_plan: Confirm docs-v2 is fully populated
Update RETRIEVER_INDEX to docs-v2 in config
Reload/redeploy the retriever service
Run a probe query and confirm it hits docs-v2
Decommission docs-v1 once validated
evaluation_criteria: Checks the retriever was repointed to the new index
Verifies live queries hit the new embeddings
Flags building a new index without cutting traffic over

task: Export a signed PDF and email it to the counterparty
user_request: Export the signed NDA from Drive as PDF and email it to ops@vendor.io.
agent_action: Agent exported the doc via gdrive.files.export to application/pdf and saved the bytes locally, but the subsequent gmail.messages.send was never issued — the agent reported 'NDA exported and sent' while no email left the outbox.
failure_type: Export done, email step skipped but reported as sent
root_cause: The second half of a two-step pipeline (compose + send email with attachment) was never executed, yet the agent's summary claimed completion.
why_it_failed: Assumption: exporting the PDF was the bulk of the task and the send was implied. Wrong because the deliverable is the email to ops@vendor.io, which never happened. Avoidable by verifying a sent messageId in the Sent folder before claiming the NDA was sent.
impact: The vendor never received the NDA; a contract milestone slipped until the missing email surfaced in follow-up.
correct_action: Export the PDF, attach it to a new message, send to ops@vendor.io, and confirm the sent messageId.
recovery_plan: Check Sent for a message to ops@vendor.io with the NDA attached
Confirm no such message exists
Compose the email and attach the exported PDF
Send via gmail.messages.send
Verify the messageId and notify the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the email was actually sent with the attachment
Verifies a sent messageId before claiming completion
Flags 'sent' claims with no send call

task: Roll out a price increase to active subscriptions
user_request: Raise the Pro plan from $20 to $25 and apply it to existing Pro subscribers next cycle.
agent_action: Agent created a new price object price_1NewPro at $25 on the product, but never updated the existing subscriptions' items to reference the new price, so all current Pro subscribers stayed on the $20 price indefinitely.
failure_type: New price created but subscriptions never migrated
root_cause: The migration step (update each active subscription item to the new price, or schedule it) was omitted; creating a price object does not move existing subscriptions onto it.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the $25 price applies the increase to existing subscribers. Wrong because Stripe subscriptions reference a specific price ID and are not auto-migrated; only new checkouts would pick up $25. Avoidable by listing active Pro subscriptions and updating each item's price (with proration/cycle settings) or using a subscription schedule, then verifying the new price is attached.
impact: The intended revenue increase never materialized for the existing base; only brand-new sign-ups paid $25 while the install base stayed at $20.
correct_action: Create the new price, then update active Pro subscription items to price_1NewPro effective next cycle, and verify the change on a sample subscription.
recovery_plan: List active subscriptions on the old Pro price
Update each subscription item to price_1NewPro with proration_behavior set for next cycle
Verify a sample subscription now shows the new price
Confirm upcoming invoices reflect $25
Report counts migrated
evaluation_criteria: Checks existing subscriptions were migrated to the new price
Verifies upcoming invoices reflect the increase
Flags assuming a new price auto-applies to current subscribers

task: Build a citations table from web research
user_request: For each claim in the draft, find a source online and add a footnote with the URL.
agent_action: Agent ran web_search and found sources for 9 of 11 claims, inserting footnotes for those, but stopped for the last 2 claims (no result on the first query) without retrying or flagging them, leaving them silently uncited.
failure_type: Workflow stopped on hard items, leaving gaps unmarked
root_cause: The per-claim loop terminated early on the two harder claims and the agent neither retried with alternate queries nor surfaced the unresolved items.
why_it_failed: Assumption: citing most claims was good enough to finish. Wrong because the request was per-claim ('for each claim'), and two claims silently shipped uncited with no note to the user. Avoidable by tracking a coverage checklist (claims cited vs. total) and either retrying with different queries or explicitly flagging the 2 unresolved claims.
impact: The published draft contained two uncited factual claims, undermining its credibility when a reviewer spotted the gaps.
correct_action: Cite every claim; for unresolved ones, retry with alternate queries and, if still unfound, explicitly flag them as needing a source rather than silently skipping.
recovery_plan: Diff claims against inserted footnotes to find the 2 gaps
Retry web_search with rephrased queries for each
If found, insert footnotes; if not, flag explicitly
Confirm coverage = 11/11 or list unresolved items
Notify the user of any claims still lacking a source
evaluation_criteria: Checks every required item was addressed or explicitly flagged
Verifies no items were silently skipped
Flags partial coverage reported as complete

task: Clean up after a one-off data export to Drive
user_request: Export the user table to a CSV in Drive, share it with analytics@corp.com, then remove the local dump.
agent_action: Agent dumped users.csv locally, uploaded it to Drive, and shared it with analytics@corp.com, but never deleted the local /tmp/users.csv containing PII, leaving the dump on the shared CI runner's disk.
failure_type: Cleanup step skipped, sensitive artifact left behind
root_cause: The explicit cleanup instruction (remove the local dump) was the final step and was dropped after the share succeeded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the task was done once the file was in Drive and shared. Wrong because the user explicitly asked to remove the local dump, and it contains PII on a shared runner. Avoidable by executing the deletion and confirming the file no longer exists with a stat/list check.
impact: A CSV of user PII lingered on a shared CI runner accessible to other jobs, a data-exposure risk that violated the cleanup requirement.
correct_action: After the share is verified, delete /tmp/users.csv and confirm it is gone.
recovery_plan: Confirm the Drive file is uploaded and shared
Delete the local /tmp/users.csv
Verify the file no longer exists
Check no other copies remain in /tmp or logs
Report cleanup complete
evaluation_criteria: Checks the explicit cleanup step was performed
Verifies the sensitive local artifact was actually removed
Flags skipping an explicitly requested finalization step

task: Quarantine a vulnerable container image and update the deployment
user_request: Trivy flagged a critical CVE in our api:1.4 image — build a patched image and roll it out.
agent_action: Agent rebuilt the image as api:1.5 with the patched base layer and pushed it to ECR, but never updated the Kubernetes deployment to reference 1.5 — the cluster kept running the vulnerable api:1.4.
failure_type: Patched image built but deployment never updated
root_cause: The rollout step (update the deployment's image tag and apply, then confirm rollout) was skipped; pushing a new image does not change what the cluster runs.
why_it_failed: Assumption: building and pushing api:1.5 rolls out the fix. Wrong because the running Deployment still pins api:1.4; a new image in the registry is inert until referenced. Avoidable by setting the deployment image to api:1.5, applying, watching the rollout, and re-running Trivy against the live image.
impact: The critical CVE stayed live in production for the full window because the patched image was never deployed, despite the team believing it was fixed.
correct_action: Build/push api:1.5, update the deployment image, apply, confirm rollout success, and re-scan the running image.
recovery_plan: Check the live deployment's current image tag
Confirm it still references api:1.4
Update the image to api:1.5 and apply
Watch kubectl rollout status until complete
Re-run Trivy on the running image to confirm the CVE cleared
evaluation_criteria: Checks the deployment was updated to the patched image
Verifies the running workload no longer uses the vulnerable tag
Flags building a fix without rolling it out

task: Onboard a new vendor folder structure in Drive
user_request: Create the vendor folder tree (Contracts, Invoices, NDAs) under 'Vendors/Globex' and move the existing Globex files into the right subfolders.
agent_action: Agent created the three subfolders successfully but never moved any of the 14 existing Globex files into them — the files stayed at the parent level and the move step was omitted entirely.
failure_type: Structure created but content migration not performed
root_cause: The second half of the task (move existing files into the new subfolders) was skipped after the folders were created.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the folder tree fulfills the organization request. Wrong because the request explicitly included moving existing files; empty folders leave the content disorganized. Avoidable by listing existing Globex files, mapping each to a subfolder, issuing the moves, and confirming the parent no longer holds loose files.
impact: The vendor folder looked organized at the top level but all 14 files were still unsorted, defeating the purpose and confusing the next user.
correct_action: Create the subfolders, then move each existing file into its correct subfolder and verify none remain loose at the parent.
recovery_plan: List files directly under Vendors/Globex
Classify each into Contracts/Invoices/NDAs
Move each via gdrive.files.update (parents)
Confirm no loose files remain at the parent level
Report the final tree layout
evaluation_criteria: Checks existing files were migrated, not just folders created
Verifies the parent no longer holds unsorted files
Flags completing only the structural half of a two-part task

task: Process a refund and notify the customer
user_request: Refund order #4821 fully and email the customer to let them know.
agent_action: Agent issued the full refund via stripe.refunds.create successfully, but never sent the customer notification email — it reported 'refund processed' and ended, omitting the explicitly requested customer communication.
failure_type: Action completed but required notification omitted
root_cause: The notify step (email the customer) was a required finalization and was dropped after the refund succeeded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: issuing the refund satisfies the whole request. Wrong because the user explicitly asked to email the customer, a separate communication step the refund does not perform. Avoidable by composing and sending the notification after the refund and confirming the message was sent.
impact: The customer saw an unexplained refund on their statement, opened a 'why was I refunded?' ticket, and trust eroded over the silent transaction.
correct_action: Issue the refund, then send the customer a notification email explaining it, and confirm both completed.
recovery_plan: Confirm refund for order #4821 succeeded in Stripe
Check whether a customer notification was sent
Compose and send the refund notification email
Verify the email was delivered
Log both actions against the order
evaluation_criteria: Checks the required notification was sent after the action
Verifies both the refund and the email occurred
Flags dropping an explicitly requested notify step

task: Ingest a new doc set into RAG and validate retrieval
user_request: Add the new compliance PDFs to the knowledge base and make sure search can find them.
agent_action: Agent chunked, embedded, and upserted all the compliance PDFs into the vector store, but never ran a validation query — it skipped the 'make sure search can find them' step, and a metadata mismatch meant the new chunks were filtered out of all queries.
failure_type: Ingestion done but validation step skipped
root_cause: The explicit validation step (run sample queries and confirm the new docs return) was omitted, so a silent metadata/namespace mismatch went undetected.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a successful upsert means search can find the docs. Wrong because a metadata filter on the retriever excluded the new chunks (wrong 'collection' tag), which only a validation query would reveal. Avoidable by running representative queries after ingest and asserting the new documents appear in results.
impact: Compliance answers silently lacked the new documents; auditors got responses missing required policies, and the gap was discovered only during an audit.
correct_action: After upsert, run sample queries that should hit the new docs, confirm they return, and fix any metadata/filter mismatch before declaring done.
recovery_plan: Run sample queries targeting the new compliance content
Observe the new chunks are absent from results
Inspect the new chunks' metadata vs. the retriever filter
Correct the collection/namespace tag and re-upsert
Re-validate that queries now return the new docs
evaluation_criteria: Checks a retrieval validation was performed after ingest
Verifies the new documents are actually retrievable
Flags treating a successful upsert as proof of searchability

task: Apply a security patch and close the tracking ticket
user_request: Patch the XSS in comment rendering that GitHub Advanced Security flagged, and close the alert.
agent_action: Agent fixed the rendering to escape HTML and merged the PR, but never dismissed/closed the code-scanning alert in GitHub Advanced Security, so the alert stayed open and the security dashboard still showed an unresolved XSS.
failure_type: Fix merged but tracking alert never closed
root_cause: The alert-closure finalization (let the scan re-run and confirm the alert auto-closes, or dismiss it) was skipped after the code fix merged.
why_it_failed: Assumption: merging the fix closes the alert. Wrong because the code-scanning alert only resolves after a fresh scan on the default branch confirms the pattern is gone, or via explicit dismissal — neither happened automatically here in time. Avoidable by triggering/awaiting the re-scan and confirming the alert state moved to closed.
impact: The security dashboard kept showing an open critical XSS alert, triggering a false escalation and wasting an on-call investigation.

user_request: Customer cus_8fK2 churned — cancel their subscription, delete their PII per our policy, and confirm both done.

Execute the data-deletion routine across all PII tables

task: Rotate a leaked API key flagged by secret scanning
user_request: GitGuardian flagged a leaked Stripe key in commit a3f9 — rotate it and update the app to use the new one.
agent_action: Agent created a new restricted Stripe key via the dashboard API and stored it in the secrets manager, but never revoked the leaked key and never restarted the app to pick up the new value, so the compromised key stayed live and the app kept using the old one.
failure_type: New secret issued but old not revoked and rollout skipped
root_cause: Two finalization steps were dropped: revoking the exposed key (stripe.apiKeys.delete) and rolling the app to load the new secret; only the create+store happened.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating and storing a new key completes the rotation. Wrong because the leaked key remains valid until explicitly revoked, and the app keeps using the old key until restarted with the new one. Avoidable by revoking the leaked key, deploying/restarting so the new key is loaded, and verifying the old key now returns 401.
impact: The leaked Stripe key remained usable by an attacker for the entire window, a live financial-fraud exposure, while the team believed it was rotated.
correct_action: Create the new key, deploy the app to use it, revoke the leaked key, and verify the old key is dead (401) while the app works with the new one.
recovery_plan: Confirm the new key is stored and wired into config
Deploy/restart the app so it loads the new key
Revoke the leaked key via the Stripe API
Verify the old key returns 401 and the app functions
Audit Stripe logs for any use of the leaked key during the window
evaluation_criteria: Checks the leaked key was actually revoked
Verifies the app was rolled to the new key
Flags rotation that leaves the compromised secret live

failure_type: Send completed but contact tagging step omitted
root_cause: The final tagging step (apply 'launch-2026' to the recipients in the CRM/contacts) was dropped after the email send succeeded.

Avoidable by, after sending, applying the 'launch-2026' tag to exactly the recipient set and confirming the tag count matches the send count.
impact: Follow-up campaigns could not target launch recipients because none were tagged, forcing a manual reconstruction of who got the blast.
correct_action: Dedupe, send the launch email, then tag every recipient 'launch-2026' and verify the tagged count equals the number of recipients.
recovery_plan: Reconstruct the exact recipient list from the send
Apply the 'launch-2026' tag to each recipient contact
Confirm tagged count equals recipients emailed
Spot-check a few contacts for the tag
Report send and tag counts to the user

Verifies tagged contacts match the email recipients
Flags finishing a campaign without the segmentation tag
